body:
That's going to be a tough one to crack without a reproduction case :(
On Jan 31, 2015 1:20 PM, "titovmaxim" notifications@github.com wrote:

> I've just published the game build with libGDX & roboVM for iOS devices.
> I've tested the game locally on simulator and iPhone-5s - everything works
> fine. However I've got plenty (several hundreds) of crash reports by Flurry
> from the game in the field:
> 
> **\* Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NullPointerException: null', reason: 'NullPointerException: null
> 
> com.badlogic.gdx.backends.iosrobovm.IOSSound.play(IOSSound.java:66)
> 
> com.badlogic.gdx.backends.iosrobovm.IOSSound.play(IOSSound.java:56)
> 
> com.mmxgames.engine.audio.RandomSound.playAtIndex(RandomSound.java:47)
> 
> com.mmxgames.engine.audio.RandomSound.play(RandomSound.java:36)
> 
> com.mmxgames.engine.audio.SoundPack.play(SoundPack.java:53)
> 
> com.mmxgames.engine.audio.SoundPack.play(SoundPack.java:37)
> 
> com.mmxgames.engine.ResMan$RSoundPack.play(ResMan.java:205)
> 
> com.mmxgames.ttj.themes.GameView3D.onMove(GameView3D.java:360)
> 
> com.mmxgames.ttj.play.ALevelScene.processAction(ALevelScene.java:356)
> 
> com.mmxgames.ttj.play.ALevelScene.__update(ALevelScene.java:186)
> 
> com.mmxgames.ttj.play.StoryLevelScene.__update(StoryLevelScene.java:144)
> 
> com.mmxgames.engine.components.Host.__update(Host.java:235)
> 
> com.mmxgames.engine.AGame.render(AGame.java:282)
> 
> com.badlogic.gdx.backends.iosrobovm.IOSGraphics.draw(IOSGraphics.java:330)
> 
> com.badlogic.gdx.backends.iosrobovm.IOSGraphics$1.draw(IOSGraphics.java:200)
> 
> org.robovm.apple.uikit.UIView.$cb$drawRect$(UIView.java)
> 
> org.robovm.apple.uikit.UIApplication.main(Native Method)
> 
> org.robovm.apple.uikit.UIApplication.main(UIApplication.java:334)
> 
> com.bulkypix.tedthejumper.ios.Launcher.main(Launcher.java:182)
> 
> So the exception raise for more or less any device type (iPhone 6 Plus,
> iPhone 6, iPhone 5s, iPhone 4s, iPads, etc.). The source code line is:
> 
> ALSource soundSource = OALSimpleAudio.sharedInstance().playEffect(soundPath, volume, pitch, pan, loop);
> 
> Only the possibility I see is that OALSimpleAudio.sharedInstance() returns
> null.
> 
> What could be the problem for that?
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/issues/2790.
I guess. But this is the error from the field. Actually a lot of (more than 300 reports!). But it is not reproducible on my device...

Maybe you have a friend with a different device to test on? I'm afraid i'm
not sure how to reproduce it.
On Jan 31, 2015 2:09 PM, "titovmaxim" notifications@github.com wrote:

> I guess. But this is the error from the field. Actually a lot of (more
> than 300 reports!). But it is not reproducible on my device...
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/issues/2790#issuecomment-72317183.

Unfortunately I have used all available devices to test prior release. Everything was fine. Last day the game start to go in China (about 5000 users) and I've got about 500 (now it is even more than 300) of such error reports by Flurry. No idea what to do except just to wrap Sound.play in try/catch with reporting to prevent fatal crashes at least.

At the moment there is about 2000 crashes with this issue. But all of them are "in the field". Is it possible to look inside OALSimpleAudio and try to understand under circumstances .sharedInstance() could return null? I'm not sure where the sources are.

We bind here https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/backends/gdx-backend-robovm/src/com/badlogic/gdx/backends/iosrobovm/objectal/OALSimpleAudio.java#L38

Which calls the native method sharedInstance, which is generated by 
https://github.com/kstenerud/ObjectAL-for-iPhone/blob/master/ObjectAL/ObjectAL/OALSimpleAudio.h#L210

I've look at the files. I'm not good in Objective C. But I see quite some possibilities when .sharedInstance() could return nil (which is converted to null then, I suppose). If _sharedInstance becomes nil (not only for first run, for whatever reason) the SynthesizeSingleton.h macros will try to create new instance by
https://github.com/kstenerud/ObjectAL-for-iPhone/blob/01c375c0803dc3c0d8aa604bc1311c8807bce3a9/ObjectAL/ObjectAL/Support/SynthesizeSingleton.h#L117

which will lead to
https://github.com/kstenerud/ObjectAL-for-iPhone/blob/master/ObjectAL/ObjectAL/OALSimpleAudio.m#L144

And this method do has several paths to return nil (with logging or without). So, as I see in the field, OALSimpleAudio.sharedInstance() could return null which leads to a crash. I could not go deeper and understand WHY it can fail (ALDevice, ALContext, etc. are out of my knowledge), but it will be at least good to:
1. Either check if sharedInstance is null and, fox example, throw the exception (not Runtime) and mark the method as throws. So one will must to wrap the calls in try/catch and to process error. 
2. Check if sharedInstance is null, ignore sound without crashing return false from the .play method and set some kind field like "lastError" in order to give the user chance to understand what happens.

Otherwise the usage is not crash-prone. The second option is better in my opinion.

Even better would not to report (sharedInstance == null), but to grab the reason from inside OALSimpleAudio.m to understand better what happens. It loggin is not enough when the crash happens remotely - one can not see it in crash reports.
Anything above and including warning level should be logged by default.
You are right. I'm sure it is logged. And it is great when you can see the logs. But the crash happens by the user side. And you get just null pointer exception. Without information which was logged.

This just shouldn't fail at all. Maybe we should bring it up with the
ObjectAL guy.

Are we 100% that the shared instance is null?
No. But I do not have any other idea why this line could lead to null pointer exception.
If only we could replicate :/ Do you have the device details for the crash reports you have received?
Cool. So how often are you playing sounds?

It's just a puzzle game. The sound plays every time the hero jump or the rain drops. So I'd say from several times per second to once per several second. I could not say that it is often. You can estimate it by looking video:
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j3sFVAGFQqo&spfreload=10

Great, thanks @titovmaxim . I'm pretty sure that ALSource is null. Not sure why you are getting an error on that line though.  

What version of LibGDX are you using?

I was able to replicate by playing sounds in very quick succession. This causes playEffect to return null, I must have missed that documentation when I implemented this, I thought it would just return -1. Alas,
this should resolve this issue, if not we can re-open.

Thanks Tomski!
